device.name: Easy DRL Isaac Sim (random_walk, Jetbot, discrete)

facts.text: The README requires Isaac Sim 2021.2.1 and installs the library by copying DRL_Isaac_lib into the Isaac Sim package directory
Isaac_envs is a gym.Env whose metadata declares render.modes human
The constructor defaults are skip_frame 1, physics_dt 1/60 s, rendering_dt 1/60 s, max_episode_length 3000, seed 0 and headless True
The step interval is stored as physics_dt * skip_frame and the reset offset as int(rendering_dt / physics_dt)
The constructor hardcodes env_name random_walk, robot_name jetbot and action_type discrete
For random_walk the constructor builds the fixed vertical path map with random=False, then draws a random robot pose and target
get_action_space returns spaces.Discrete(3) for the discrete action type
The observation space is a Dict of three Boxes: IR_raleted shape (1,12) in [0,1], pos_raleted shape (2,) low [0,-pi] high [8,pi], and vel_raleted shape (2,) low [0,-pi/4] high [10,pi/4]
The Jetbot's three discrete movements are [15, 0.785], [25, 0] and [15, -0.785], each a [linear, yaw] pair
The differential controller uses wheel radius 3.25 and wheel base 11.25 for the Jetbot and computes the two wheel joint velocities from the [linear, yaw] command

step applies the selected movement for each skip frame, calls differential_controller for a differential robot, advances the world with world.step(render=False), and returns (observations, reward, done, info)
The observation is the lidar ranges, the goal distance and angular difference, and the base linear and angular velocity
The lidar interface resizes its depth array to (1, number_lasers)
distance_to measures the 3D Euclidean distance and angular_difference_to computes theta from the quaternion components and returns a wrapped theta-alpha angle
The episode ends when current_time_step_index - steps_after_reset reaches max_episode_length, when the minimum lidar range is <= 0.155, or when the goal distance is <= 0.5

The reward starts as distance_reward = -distance/100 and is scaled by 1 - index/max_episode_length only when distance_reward is positive, minus 10*(0.6 - minimum_lidar) on a lidar collision, and plus 10 + 90*(1 - index/max_episode_length) at the goal
reset calls world.reset() and, for random_walk, randomizes the goal position and then the robot pose; it returns only the observation
The seed method uses gym.utils.seeding.np_random(seed), calls np.random.seed(seed) and returns [seed]
The lidar is created with 12 lasers, a 360-degree horizontal FOV, a 30-degree vertical FOV, 360/number_lasers horizontal resolution, rotation_rate 0 and yaw_offset 0
For the Jetbot the lidar min_range is 0.15 and max_range is 1
The random_walk map uses map_dist_unit 0.5 and height 0.2 for the Jetbot, a 5x5 grid, four outer walls and one cube for every grid cell
The fixed map array is rotated counter-clockwise with np.rot90, and a cell is visible when its rotated value is 1

The random reset draws the robot x as map_dist_unit * randint(map_dimension), its y as -1.5*map_dist_unit and its orientation quaternion as [0, 0, sin(a), cos(a)] with a = rand()*pi; the goal x is drawn the same way with y = 5.5*map_dist_unit and z = 0.25
get_observations acquires depth camera data but does not use it; the returned dictionary contains only IR_raleted, pos_raleted and vel_raleted
render returns without drawing and close closes the SimulationApp

determinism.notes: cap.world.seed.v1 or cap.world.reset.v1(seed) seeds the fake's Python random.Random before the reset; upstream seed() uses gym.utils.seeding.np_random and numpy's global generator (env.py:249-252) while the fake draws with random.Random, so one seed does not reproduce upstream trajectories; neither path was compared with the other

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in: the commanded [linear, yaw] velocity is integrated directly at the default 1/60 s control period; there is no Isaac Sim/PhysX rigid-body dynamics, wheel-ground friction, actuator response, gravity, contact response or rendering, so the deployed model is F0 (absence of dynamics) even though the upstream uses Isaac Sim 2021.2.1 (README.md:70)

the fake's linear command gain of 0.01 is a placeholder, not a verified centimetre-to-metre conversion; the controller at isaac_robots.py:142-163 states wheel geometry and wheel velocity formulas but no linear command unit

the goal-angle calculation preserves isaac_robots.py:245-259: for the fake's planar quaternion [0, 0, sin(yaw/2), cos(yaw/2)], the pinned theta numerator is zero and theta is pi rather than yaw; the simulator's quaternion convention was not validated

the 12-beam lidar is an analytic 2D raycast against the fixed random_walk obstacle boxes, capped at 1 m and clamped to 0.15 m; the Isaac range sensor's exact beam phase, vertical FOV, 3D occlusion and miss behaviour are not modelled
the RGB/depth camera data is acquired by get_observations (env.py:218) but is not part of the returned observation or the observation space (env.py:113-120); NOT COVERED: the RGB/depth camera arrays

the random reset draws the robot x and yaw and the goal x with Python's random.Random from the same distributions as isaac_envs.py:409-430; upstream draws them from numpy's global generator seeded by seed() (env.py:249-252), so a seed gives different trajectories on the two, and observations are Python lists rather than numpy arrays

the fake was never compared with the upstream environment: Isaac Sim 2021.2.1 is proprietary (README.md:70) and is not installed or importable where the gate runs; there is no SyntheticDataHelper and no rendering

the environment is not registered with Gymnasium and no simulator backend is listed: the upstream is installed only by copying it into an Isaac Sim 2021.2.1 tree (README.md:70-74), so this package serves the fake backend only

a live wrapper would need its own lifecycle and output handling: the upstream constructor starts SimulationApp and uses flat module imports (env.py:27-37), reset prints to stdout (env.py:207-210), the goal branch prints to stdout (env.py:185-189), and close closes SimulationApp (env.py:245-247); the fake latch supplies no stop for an independently running Isaac timeline
snapshot and restore are not offered: Isaac_envs exposes no get_state/set_state method

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the served fake stops advancing: the latch refuses step and world-reset commands until mhs.safety.reset clears it; the fake state stays readable. This package serves no Isaac Sim backend and controls no external simulator timeline
